[LLM] Kopia process spawns ssh with -oProxyCommand= argument (CVE-2026-45695) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of Kopia's unauthenticated SFTP/externalSSH path injection. When the vulnerable /api/v1/repo/exists handler invokes blob.NewStorage with attacker-supplied sshArguments, the kopia process directly forks ssh with a -oProxyCommand= token that OpenSSH then executes via $SHELL -c. The kopia→ssh parent/child with ProxyCommand in the child argv is a near-zero-FP signature of this RCE. Rationale: Uses the exact narrow signature described in the advisory: kopia process (vulnerable handler) directly invoking exec.CommandContext("ssh", ...) with a ProxyCommand token. The string 'ProxyCommand' in an ssh argv whose parent is kopia has effectively no benign use case outside intentional SFTP jump-host setups. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, the Kopia v0.22.3 source references in the article, and the fix PR #5354. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354 • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/blob/v0.22.3/repo/blob/sftp/sftp_storage.go • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45695
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] SSH process spawned by Kopia invokes a shell child (ProxyCommand execution) Installation High
Detects the second-stage execution arm of CVE-2026-45695: OpenSSH evaluates -oProxyCommand=<cmd> by invoking $SHELL -c <cmd> before any TCP connect. The resulting kopia → ssh → (sh|bash|cmd|powershell) grand-parent/parent/child chain is the artifact of arbitrary code running as the kopia service account. Rationale: This is the exact execution chain the advisory describes — OpenSSH spawns $SHELL -c <attacker_cmd> before attempting TCP, so the shell child of ssh is the observable smoking gun. Pairing it with a kopia grand-parent (via SshPid join) removes essentially all benign ssh ProxyCommand use. Confirmed against the GHSA advisory text and OpenSSH ProxyCommand documented behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2q4c-3mrw-63c3 • https://man.openbsd.org/ssh_config.5#ProxyCommand • https://github.com/kopia/kopia/pull/5354
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1203

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),

            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Installation of malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 PyPI package (CVE-2026-45758) Delivery High
Hunts pip/uv/poetry invocations that pin or resolve to the quarantined guardrails-ai 0.10.1 release. Any host that ran this install must be treated as compromised because the malicious code executes on package import, not just install. Rationale: Pivots on the exact malicious release pin string `guardrails-ai==0.10.1` named in the GHSA advisory. SafeDep + Qualys confirm the 0.10.1 PyPI artifact runs malicious code on import; any host that installed it is presumed compromised regardless of whether the dropper fired. Casing variations are covered for path matches. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/issues/1473 • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or ProcessCommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "0.10.1"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

(

  | where EventID == 4688

     or ParentProcessName has_any ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","uv.exe","poetry.exe")
  | where CommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or CommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
  | where CommandLine has "0.10.1"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3","uv","poetry")
     or TargetProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","uv","poetry")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "guardrails-ai" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "guardrails_ai"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "0.10.1"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Installation of Malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 PyPI Package (CVE-2026-45758)
id: 8c41a2f9-3b76-4e2d-9e1a-7f1c5a9d4e21
description: Detects pip / uv / poetry / python invocations that install or resolve the malicious guardrails-ai==0.10.1 release published 2026-05-11 (TeamPCP supply-chain attack).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmpw-2vmm-p4p6
  - https://github.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/issues/1473
  - https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.006
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\pip.exe'
      - '\pip3.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\pythonw.exe'
      - '\uv.exe'
      - '\poetry.exe'
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/uv'
      - '/poetry'
  selection_pkg:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'guardrails-ai==0.10.1'
      - 'guardrails-ai-0.10.1'
      - 'guardrails_ai-0.10.1'
      - 'guardrails-ai 0.10.1'
  condition: selection_tool and selection_pkg
falsepositives:
  - Intentional analyst download of the quarantined artifact in an isolated reverse-engineering sandbox
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd) (@Image:(*\\pip.exe OR *\\pip3.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\uv.exe OR *\\poetry.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/pip OR */pip3 OR */python OR */python3 OR */uv OR */poetry)) AND (@CommandLine:(*guardrails-ai==0.10.1* OR *guardrails-ai-0.10.1* OR *guardrails_ai-0.10.1*) OR @process.command_line:(*guardrails-ai==0.10.1* OR *guardrails-ai-0.10.1* OR *guardrails_ai-0.10.1*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(pip|pip3|python|python3|pythonw|uv|poetry)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("guardrails[-_]ai[ =-]+0\.10\.1", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=collect([CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName]))

[LLM] Python process executing transformers.pyz dropped from git-tanstack.com (TeamPCP) Installation High
Hunts the post-import dropper stage: a python interpreter invoked with the staged payload filename `transformers.pyz` or writing that file to disk. This is the second-stage execution from the malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 __init__.py and is shared with the broader TanStack/Mistral mini-Shai-Hulud campaign. Rationale: SafeDep + Qualys reverse-engineered the malicious `guardrails/__init__.py` and identified the exact dropper filename `transformers.pyz` pulled from git-tanstack.com and executed via python3. `.pyz` is a Python zipapp — a high-signal extension on a process command line because legitimate transformers (HuggingFace) ships as a wheel, not a zipapp. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/ • https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-170-packages-hit-across-npm-pypi/
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006 T1195.002

     or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python","python3")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ActionType="ProcessCreate"
),
(
  DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where FileName =~ "transformers.pyz"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ActionType

| order by Timestamp desc

union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImProcessCreate

  | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","pythonw")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImProcessCreate"
),
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

title: Python Execution of transformers.pyz Dropper (TeamPCP / guardrails-ai 0.10.1)
id: 5a9e1d4b-2c87-4f55-8e3a-1d4a6b8e2c14
description: Detects a python interpreter invoked with the second-stage payload filename transformers.pyz used by the TeamPCP supply-chain campaign behind the malicious guardrails-ai 0.10.1 PyPI release (CVE-2026-45758) and the parallel TanStack/Mistral npm compromises.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmpw-2vmm-p4p6
  - https://safedep.io/mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-tanstack-mistral/
  - https://qualysec.com/cybersecurity-news/mini-shai-hulud-worm-compromises/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_python:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\pythonw.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/pythonw'
  selection_payload:
    CommandLine|contains: 'transformers.pyz'
  condition: selection_python and selection_payload
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate HuggingFace transformers library packaged as a zipapp (extremely uncommon — transformers ships as a regular wheel, not a .pyz)
level: high

[LLM] zrok ProxyShare SSRF — request path begins with absolute URL (CVE-2026-45568) Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to a zrok Python ProxyShare where the request path itself is an absolute URL (http:// or https://) — the precise shape of the CVE-2026-45568 SSRF, including pivots to cloud metadata services like 127.0.0.1:19190/metadata. Article-specific because Flask + urllib.parse.urljoin only rewrites the host when the second argument is absolute, so this URI shape is the exact attacker vector. Rationale: Article specifies the exact SSRF primitive: a request path that itself is an absolute URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:19190/metadata) bypasses urljoin's base-URL anchoring. The Sentinel union targets the two web-server log tables actually populated for App Service and IIS-hosted zrok deployments; the Defender query pivots on the resulting outbound proxy call to link-local / loopback metadata IPs since Defender doesn't expose web access logs. Cross-checked GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 and the urllib.parse.urljoin RFC-3986 absolute-URI behaviour documented at docs.python.org. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jh67-hwqw-m5r7 • https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.parse.html#urllib.parse.urljoin • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-45568
ATT&CKT1190 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting has no native web-server log table; this detection lives in IIS / AppService / WAF logs and is expressed on Sentinel side.
// Closest Defender pivot: any process on a zrok-hosting endpoint making an outbound connection to a link-local / loopback metadata IP shortly after receiving inbound traffic on the share.
let MetadataIPs = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2","fd00:ec2::254","100.100.100.200"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("zrok.exe","zrok","python.exe","python3","python","pythonw.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("zrok share","ProxyShare","zrok.proxy","urllib.parse.urljoin")
| where RemoteIP in (MetadataIPs) or RemoteIP startswith "169.254."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
// Hunt inbound HTTP requests where the URI itself is an absolute URL (the zrok ProxyShare SSRF shape).
let Lookback = 7d;
let AbsoluteUrlPath = @"(?i)^/+https?:/";
let MetadataMarkers = dynamic(["127.0.0.1","169.254.169.254","metadata.google","metadata.azure","100.100.100.200","/metadata","/latest/meta-data","/computeMetadata"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or csUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer,
              ClientIP = cIP, Method = csMethod,
              UriStem = csUriStem, UriQuery = csUriQuery,
              Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent,
              SourceTable = "W3CIISLog"
),
(
    AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where CsUriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath
         or CsUriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers)
    | project TimeGenerated, _ResourceId, Computer = CsHost,
              ClientIP = CIp, Method = CsMethod,
              UriStem = CsUriStem, UriQuery = CsUriQuery,
              Status = ScStatus, UserAgent = UserAgent,
              SourceTable = "AppServiceHTTPLogs"
)
| extend AbsoluteUrlInPath = iff(UriStem matches regex AbsoluteUrlPath, true, false)
| extend MetadataTargeted = iff(UriStem has_any (MetadataMarkers) or UriQuery has_any (MetadataMarkers), true, false)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exposing Fox Tempest: A malware-signing service operation

2026-05-19 16 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

[LLM] Fox Tempest signed-payload SHA256 hash execution Installation High
Detects execution, load, or write of binaries whose SHA256 hashes are attributed by Microsoft Threat Intelligence to Fox Tempest's malware-signing-as-a-service (MSaaS) operation. These two hashes are documented Fox Tempest-signed payloads delivered May 2026 in active intrusions enabling Rhysida/INC/Akira ransomware affiliates. Rationale: Hashes f0668ce... and 11af4566... are the two SHA256 IOCs published in the article's IOC table (Table 2) with last-seen dates of 2026-05-04 / 2026-05-07 — directly attributable to Fox Tempest-signed binaries delivered by Vanilla Tempest / Storm-0501 / Storm-0249 ransomware affiliates. Unioning ProcessExec + ImageLoad + FileWrite catches the payload whether it ran as a top-level process, was sideloaded as a DLL, or just landed on disk pre-detonation.
ATT&CKT1553.002 T1036.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
// Hunt for Fox Tempest-attributed SHA256 hashes across execution, image load, and file write
let FoxTempestHashes = dynamic([
    "f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc",
    "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326"]);
let Lookback = 90d;
union
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, EvidenceSurface = "ProcessExec",
           FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceImageLoadEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
           EvidenceSurface = "ImageLoad",
           FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
           ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
           EvidenceSurface = "FileWrite",
           FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
           ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| order by Timestamp desc
let FoxTempestHashes = dynamic([
    "f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc",
    "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326"]);
union
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where SHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EvidenceSurface = "ProcessExec",
           ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
           ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine),
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
 | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (FoxTempestHashes)

           ParentProcessName = "", ParentProcessCommandLine = "")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Endpoint communication to Fox Tempest MSaaS portal signspace.cloud Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP(S) egress to signspace.cloud, the Fox Tempest malware-signing-as-a-service portal disrupted by Microsoft DCU in May 2026. Any historical or stale endpoint contacting this domain indicates either a Fox Tempest customer (i.e. compromise actor) or a Fox Tempest-signed payload still beaconing for refresh. Rationale: signspace[.]cloud is named in the article body as Fox Tempest's MSaaS portal and is the sole domain in IOC Table 2 (Type=Domain, first-seen 2025-05-29, last-seen 2026-05-05). The 365-day lookback aligns with the portal's full operational window. Process-context fields surface which binary on the endpoint initiated the contact — a browser hit suggests an actor accessing the portal, a non-browser hit suggests a Fox Tempest-signed payload phoning home.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Proxy
// Fox Tempest MSaaS portal contact — signspace.cloud was active 2025-05-29 to 2026-05-05
let Lookback = 365d;
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where RemoteUrl has "signspace.cloud" or RemoteUrl has "signspace[.]cloud"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EvidenceSurface = "Network",
           InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
           InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
 | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse", "ConnectionSuccess")
 | where RemoteUrl has "signspace.cloud" or AdditionalFields has "signspace.cloud"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EvidenceSurface = ActionType,
           InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
           InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
           RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 365d;
union
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
 | where DnsQuery has "signspace.cloud"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
           EvidenceSurface = "DNS",
           DnsQuery, DnsQueryTypeName, DnsResponseName),
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
 | where Url has "signspace.cloud" or HttpHostName has "signspace.cloud"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
           EvidenceSurface = "Web",
           DnsQuery = HttpHostName, DnsQueryTypeName = "", DnsResponseName = Url),
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
 | where RequestURL has "signspace.cloud" or DestinationDnsDomain has "signspace.cloud"

           SrcUsername = SourceUserName, EvidenceSurface = "Proxy",
           DnsQuery = DestinationDnsDomain, DnsQueryTypeName = "",
           DnsResponseName = RequestURL)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Masqueraded AnyDesk/PuTTY/Webex binary with non-canonical publisher metadata Delivery Medium
Hunts for processes named or branded as AnyDesk/PuTTY/Webex/Teams whose PE version-info company name does NOT match the canonical software vendor, surfacing Fox Tempest-signed malware abusing the MSaaS pipeline to ship trojanised look-alikes of the four legitimate products explicitly called out in the article. Pairs masquerade-name with company-name mismatch to suppress legitimate enterprise repackaging. Rationale: Article body explicitly enumerates the four products Fox Tempest masquerades signed payloads as: AnyDesk, Teams, Putty, and Webex. Pairing the legitimate filename / product-name with a publisher-mismatch and out-of-canonical-path narrows to genuine masquerade attempts and excludes real vendor installs that live in Program Files with the matching publisher. Teams is intentionally excluded from the company-name check (legitimate Teams IS signed by Microsoft, same as the Fox Tempest-abused Artifact Signing service — that pair is indistinguishable on cert metadata alone and would generate too many FPs).
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1553.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Hunt: binaries masquerading as AnyDesk / PuTTY / Webex per Fox Tempest's stated targets
// Article: "masquerade as legitimate software (like AnyDesk, Teams, Putty, and Webex)"
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("anydesk.exe", "putty.exe", "webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe")
   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AnyDesk", "PuTTY", "Webex")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// Expected canonical company-name per product (verified against vendor releases)
| extend ExpectedCompany = case(
    FileName =~ "anydesk.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "AnyDesk", "AnyDesk Software GmbH",
    FileName =~ "putty.exe"  or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "PuTTY",   "Simon Tatham",
    FileName in~ ("webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe") or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "Webex", "Cisco",
    "")
| where ExpectedCompany != ""
| where isempty(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName) or not(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has ExpectedCompany)
// Exclude canonical Program Files install locations
| where not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\AnyDesk")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\AnyDesk")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\PuTTY")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\PuTTY")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\Cisco\Webex")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Cisco\Webex")
    and not(FolderPath startswith @"C:\Program Files\Webex")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ClaimedProduct = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ClaimedCompany = ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName,
          ExpectedCompany, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel: same masquerade hunt via ASIM ImProcessCreate
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("anydesk.exe", "putty.exe", "webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe")
   or ActingProcessFileProduct has_any ("AnyDesk", "PuTTY", "Webex")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend ExpectedCompany = case(
    ActingProcessName has "anydesk.exe" or ActingProcessFileProduct has "AnyDesk", "AnyDesk Software GmbH",
    ActingProcessName has "putty.exe"  or ActingProcessFileProduct has "PuTTY",   "Simon Tatham",
    ActingProcessName has_any ("webex.exe", "webexmta.exe", "webexteams.exe", "webexhost.exe") or ActingProcessFileProduct has "Webex", "Cisco",
    "")
| where ExpectedCompany != ""
| where isempty(ActingProcessFileCompany) or not(ActingProcessFileCompany has ExpectedCompany)
| where not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files\AnyDesk")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\AnyDesk")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files\PuTTY")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\PuTTY")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files\Cisco\Webex")
    and not(ActingProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Cisco\Webex")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          ClaimedProduct = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          ClaimedCompany = ActingProcessFileCompany,
          ExpectedCompany, SHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\anydesk.exe OR *\\AnyDesk.exe OR *\\putty.exe OR *\\PuTTY.exe OR *\\webex.exe OR *\\Webex.exe OR *\\webexmta.exe OR *\\webexteams.exe OR *\\webexhost.exe) OR @Product:(AnyDesk OR PuTTY OR Webex)) -@Image:(*\\Program?Files\\AnyDesk\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\PuTTY\\* OR *\\Program?Files\\Cisco\\Webex\\* OR *\\Program?Files?(x86)\\AnyDesk\\* OR *\\Program?Files?(x86)\\PuTTY\\* OR *\\Program?Files?(x86)\\Cisco\\Webex\\*) -@Company:("AnyDesk Software GmbH" OR "Simon Tatham" OR "Cisco Systems, Inc." OR "Cisco WebEx LLC")
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(anydesk|putty|webex|webexmta|webexteams|webexhost)\.exe$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\Program Files( \(x86\))?\\(AnyDesk|PuTTY|Cisco\\Webex|Webex)\\/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

level: high

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High

ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027

DeviceProcessEvents

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution

status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or SHA1 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or MD5 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or SHA1 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63") or MD5 in~ ("f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f0668ce925f36ff7f3359b0ea47e3fa243af13cd6ad9661dfccc9ff79fb4f1cc", "11af4566539ad3224e968194c7a9ad7b596460d8f6e423fc62d1ea5fc0724326", "dc0acb01e3086ea8a9cb144a5f97810d291020ce", "7e6d9dac619c04ae1b3c8c0906123e752ed66d63"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

DirtyDecrypt PoC Released for Linux Kernel CVE-2026-31635 LPE Vulnerability

The Hacker News
2026-05-19 9 use cases 3 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit code has now been released for a recently patched security flaw in the Linux kernel that could allow for local privilege escalation (LPE). Dubbed DirtyDecrypt (aka DirtyCBC), the vulnerability was discovered and reported by the Zellic and V12 security team on May 9, 2026, only to be informed by the maintainers that it was a duplicate of a vulnerability that had

CVEsCVE-2026-31635 CVE-2026-31431 CVE-2026-43284 CVE-2026-43500 CVE-2026-46300 CVE-2026-41651 CVE-2026-46333
ATT&CKT1190 T1486 T1555.003

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Linux hosts vulnerable to DirtyDecrypt / Copy Fail / Dirty Frag / Fragnesia LPE family · Article-specific behavioural hunt — DirtyDecrypt PoC Released for Linux Kernel CVE-2026-31635 LPE Vulnerability
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Linux /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers modified by non-account-management process (DirtyDecrypt post-exploit) · [LLM] Linux SUID binary modified by non-package-manager (DirtyDecrypt page-cache write outcome)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Linux ssh-keysign invoked by unprivileged user (CVE-2026-46333 ssh-keysign-pwn) · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Linux hosts vulnerable to DirtyDecrypt / Copy Fail / Dirty Frag / Fragnesia LPE family Exploitation High
Inventory Linux endpoints exposed to the page-cache COW-bypass LPE family disclosed in May 2026 (CVE-2026-31635 DirtyDecrypt, CVE-2026-31431 Copy Fail, CVE-2026-43284/43500 Dirty Frag, CVE-2026-46300 Fragnesia, CVE-2026-41651 Pack2TheRoot, CVE-2026-46333 ssh-keysign-pwn). PoC for DirtyDecrypt is public on GitHub via NVD; CONFIG_RXGK distributions (Fedora, Arch Linux, openSUSE Tumbleweed) are the priority patch targets. Rationale: Direct CVE list pulled from the article (CVE-2026-31635, -31431, -43284, -43500, -46300, -41651, -46333) plus the article's named at-risk distros (Fedora, Arch, openSUSE Tumbleweed for CONFIG_RXGK). Inventory pivot is the only reliable signal at disclosure time before in-the-wild artefacts exist.
ATT&CKT1068 T1611

| extend RxgkDistro = iff(OSPlatform has_any ("Fedora","Arch","openSUSE"),"yes","no")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), CVEs=make_set(CveId), Software=make_set(SoftwareName), Versions=make_set(SoftwareVersion), Severities=make_set(VulnerabilitySeverityLevel) by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, RxgkDistro

[LLM] Linux /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers modified by non-account-management process (DirtyDecrypt post-exploit) Installation High
Detect writes to /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, or /etc/sudoers.d/* that did NOT originate from a known account-management or package-manager binary. DirtyDecrypt (CVE-2026-31635) and the Dirty Frag/Fragnesia variants achieve root by writing through the kernel page cache into these privileged files — the on-disk artefact ultimately appears as an unexpected modifier. Rationale: Article explicitly names /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, and SUID binaries as the privileged files targeted by the page-cache COW-bypass primitive — these become the on-disk witnesses of successful exploitation of CVE-2026-31635 (DirtyDecrypt), CVE-2026-31431 (Copy Fail), CVE-2026-43284/43500 (Dirty Frag) and CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia). Allow-list of account-management binaries is the standard suppression.
ATT&CKT1068 T1098 T1222.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath == "/etc" and FileName in~ ("shadow","sudoers"))
   or FolderPath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
   or FolderPath in ("/etc/shadow","/etc/sudoers")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("passwd","chpasswd","usermod","useradd","userdel","vipw","vigr","visudo","chage","gpasswd","newusers","systemd","systemd-tmpfiles","systemd-sysusers","dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","zypper","pacman","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","salt-call","ansible-playbook","cloud-init","cfengine","sssd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath in ("/etc/shadow","/etc/sudoers")
   or TargetFilePath startswith "/etc/sudoers.d/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("passwd","chpasswd","usermod","useradd","userdel","vipw","vigr","visudo","chage","gpasswd","newusers","systemd","systemd-tmpfiles","systemd-sysusers","dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","zypper","pacman","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","salt-call","ansible-playbook","cloud-init","cfengine","sssd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: Detects writes to /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, or /etc/sudoers.d/* by a process that is NOT a known account-management or package-manager binary. Post-exploitation indicator for the DirtyDecrypt / Copy Fail / Dirty Frag / Fragnesia Linux kernel LPE family that uses page-cache COW bypasses to tamper with these files.

      - '/systemd'

level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR SYSCALL) @file.path:(/etc/shadow OR /etc/sudoers OR /etc/sudoers.d/*) -@process.executable.path:(*/passwd OR */chpasswd OR */usermod OR */useradd OR */userdel OR */vipw OR */vigr OR */visudo OR */chage OR */gpasswd OR */newusers OR */systemd OR */systemd-tmpfiles OR */systemd-sysusers OR */dpkg OR */rpm OR */yum OR */dnf OR */apt OR */apt-get OR */unattended-upgrade OR */zypper OR */pacman OR */puppet OR */chef-client OR */salt-minion OR */ansible-playbook OR */cloud-init OR */sssd)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/^\/etc\/(shadow|sudoers)(\/|$)/i OR TargetFileName=/^\/etc\/sudoers\.d\//i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\/(passwd|chpasswd|usermod|useradd|userdel|vipw|vigr|visudo|chage|gpasswd|newusers|systemd|systemd-tmpfiles|systemd-sysusers|dpkg|rpm|yum|dnf|apt|apt-get|unattended-upgrade|zypper|pacman|puppet|chef-client|salt-minion|ansible-playbook|cloud-init|sssd)$/i)

[LLM] Linux SUID binary modified by non-package-manager (DirtyDecrypt page-cache write outcome) Installation High
Detect modification of common SUID-root binaries (su, sudo, passwd, mount, pkexec, ssh-keysign, newgrp, gpasswd) by a process that is NOT a package manager or configuration-management agent. The article identifies SUID binaries as a direct page-cache write target for DirtyDecrypt and Dirty Frag — replacing one with attacker-controlled bytes yields root on next invocation. Rationale: Article calls out SUID binaries as one of the three explicit page-cache write targets named for DirtyDecrypt (alongside /etc/shadow and /etc/sudoers). Modification of a SUID-root binary by anything other than the OS package manager is one of the highest-fidelity Linux post-exploit signals available.
ATT&CKT1068 T1574 T1222.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SuidPaths = dynamic(["/usr/bin/su","/usr/bin/sudo","/usr/bin/passwd","/usr/bin/chage","/usr/bin/gpasswd","/usr/bin/newgrp","/usr/bin/mount","/usr/bin/umount","/usr/bin/pkexec","/usr/bin/at","/usr/lib/openssh/ssh-keysign","/usr/libexec/openssh/ssh-keysign","/usr/lib/policykit-1/polkit-agent-helper-1","/usr/libexec/polkit-agent-helper-1"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| extend FullPath = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName)
| where FullPath in (SuidPaths) or FolderPath in (SuidPaths)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","yum","dnf","apt","apt-get","unattended-upgrade","zypper","pacman","systemd","systemd-tmpfiles","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","ansible-playbook","cloud-init")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FullPath, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuidPaths = dynamic(["/usr/bin/su","/usr/bin/sudo","/usr/bin/passwd","/usr/bin/chage","/usr/bin/gpasswd","/usr/bin/newgrp","/usr/bin/mount","/usr/bin/umount","/usr/bin/pkexec","/usr/bin/at","/usr/lib/openssh/ssh-keysign","/usr/libexec/openssh/ssh-keysign","/usr/lib/policykit-1/polkit-agent-helper-1","/usr/libexec/polkit-agent-helper-1"]);
ImFileEvent

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Linux ssh-keysign invoked by unprivileged user (CVE-2026-46333 ssh-keysign-pwn) Actions on Objectives High
Detect ssh-keysign execution under a non-root, non-sshd user context. CVE-2026-46333 (ssh-keysign-pwn) is an improper-privilege-management flaw that lets an unprivileged local user leverage the SUID-root ssh-keysign helper to read root-owned secrets such as /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key. Legitimate ssh-keysign invocations originate from the ssh client during HostbasedAuthentication and run very rarely on most hosts. Rationale: Article names CVE-2026-46333 (aka ssh-keysign-pwn) as a SUID-helper improper-privilege-management flaw that gives unprivileged users read access to root-owned secrets including SSH private keys. Legitimate ssh-keysign is only invoked transiently by ssh during HostbasedAuthentication — any other parent + non-root user combination is a high-fidelity abuse signal.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1068 T1548.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "ssh-keysign"
   or FolderPath in ("/usr/lib/openssh","/usr/libexec/openssh")
     and FileName =~ "ssh-keysign"
| where AccountName !in~ ("root","sshd")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ssh","sshd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "ssh-keysign" or ActingProcessName endswith "ssh-keysign"
| where ActorUsername !in~ ("root","sshd")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "/ssh" and ParentProcessName !endswith "/sshd" and ParentProcessName !in~ ("ssh","sshd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 present
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: unauthenticated GET to /system/api/connectionSettings · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-46395: HAXcms: Private Key Disclosure via Broken HMAC
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: forged-JWT admin write within 30m of connectionSettings leak
[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: unauthenticated GET to /system/api/connectionSettings Exploitation High
Surfaces any HTTP GET to the HAXcms unauthenticated /system/api/connectionSettings endpoint, which returns base64 tokens whose tail bytes are the private signing key (privateKey+salt) plaintext. A single GET against a vulnerable @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs <= 25.0.0 instance fully discloses the JWT-signing secret, so any request to this path on internet-facing HAXcms deployments warrants triage. Rationale: Endpoint path `/system/api/connectionSettings` is the article-named primary leak vector and is not present on benign HAXcms traffic that goes through the authenticated UI. A successful 2xx on this path is essentially equivalent to private-key exfiltration. Defender_kql is intentionally empty because Defender Advanced Hunting does not ship raw HTTP request URIs for arbitrary Node.js applications — the detection lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://github.com/haxtheweb/issues
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = ScStatus, UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET"
        | where csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName, UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| where Status between (200 .. 299)   // 2xx = key successfully disclosed
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent, 10), Statuses = make_set(Status, 5)
            by SourceIp, Host
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] HAXcms CVE-2026-46395: forged-JWT admin write within 30m of connectionSettings leak Actions on Objectives High
Correlates a successful GET to /system/api/connectionSettings (the private-key leak primitive) with subsequent authenticated HAXcms admin-write API calls from the same source IP within 30 minutes. Because forged JWTs are signed with the stolen privateKey+salt they produce no login events and look indistinguishable from the real admin to single-event detections — this temporal correlation is the cleanest way to catch the full exploit chain. Rationale: The article describes the complete exploit chain (extract key → forge admin JWT → call admin API) as feasible "with a single HTTP request" sequence, and explicitly warns the forged tokens "produce no login events in logs". Temporal correlation of the article-named leak path (`/system/api/connectionSettings`) with the article-named admin endpoints (saveOutline / saveManifest / saveNode / createSite / deleteSite / saveFile / saveUser / form_token) from the same source IP within a tight window is the only reliable host-agnostic signal. Defender_kql is a host-tier approximation that depends on the HAXcms server itself being enrolled in Defender for Endpoint; if it is not, leave the Defender field empty operationally and rely on the Sentinel / Splunk web-tier queries. Datadog/Falcon/Sigma left empty — single-shape Sigma cannot express the cross-event join, and Falcon FDR does not ship arbitrary Node.js HTTP request URIs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6c8g-9hfh-pq5h • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-46395
ATT&CKT1606.001 T1078 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// HAXcms is a Node.js web app — the JWT/Authorization header signal lives on the web tier (AppServiceHTTPLogs / W3CIISLog), not in DeviceProcessEvents.
// On hosts that run HAXcms AND are enrolled in Defender, this query approximates the post-exploit chain by joining
// outbound DNS lookups from the suspected attacker host to HAXcms domains with subsequent file modifications under
// HAXcms content roots performed by the local node.exe.
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let HaxcmsHostHints = dynamic(["haxcms","haxtheweb"]);
let NetTouch = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (HaxcmsHostHints) or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","HttpConnectionInspected")
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\haxcms\\","/haxcms/","\\_sites\\","/_sites/","site.json","manifest.json")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| join kind=inner NetTouch on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (NetTime .. NetTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NetTime)
| project NetTime, FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP,
          FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by NetTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let WindowDays = 7d;
let HaxcmsLeak = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod =~ "GET" and csUriStem =~ "/system/api/connectionSettings"
        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project LeakTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName);
let HaxcmsAdminWrite = union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod in~ ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
        | where csUriStem has_any ("/system/api/saveOutline","/system/api/saveManifest","/system/api/saveNode","/system/api/createSite","/system/api/deleteSite","/system/api/saveFile","/system/api/saveUser","/system/api/listFiles")
        | where ScStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project WriteTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = CIp, Host = CsHost,
                  UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, UserAgent = UserAgent),
    (W3CIISLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
        | where csMethod in~ ("POST","PUT","DELETE","PATCH")
        | where csUriStem has_any ("/system/api/saveOutline","/system/api/saveManifest","/system/api/saveNode","/system/api/createSite","/system/api/deleteSite","/system/api/saveFile","/system/api/saveUser","/system/api/listFiles")
        | where scStatus between (200 .. 299)
        | project WriteTime = TimeGenerated, SourceIp = cIP, Host = sSiteName,
                  UriStem = csUriStem, Method = csMethod, UserAgent = csUserAgent);
HaxcmsLeak
| join kind=inner HaxcmsAdminWrite on SourceIp, Host
| where WriteTime between (LeakTime .. LeakTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', WriteTime, LeakTime)
| project LeakTime, WriteTime, DelaySec, SourceIp, Host, UriStem, Method, UserAgent
| order by LeakTime desc
