[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 backchannel: python polling GitHub commit search for 'firedalazer' Command & Control High
Detects Python processes reaching api.github.com/search/commits with the 'firedalazer' keyword — the C2 backchannel used by the kitty/cat.py daemon to fetch RSA-PSS-signed command payloads. Hourly poll cadence and the specific search keyword make this article-grade high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim 'polls the GitHub commit search API hourly for commands containing the keyword firedalazer'. The hourly poll cadence (PollCount >= 4 over 7d window catches the daemon while avoiding a one-off curl), python initiator with cat.py in the cmdline, and the unique 'firedalazer' keyword all combine to article-grade fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py",".local/share/kitty","kitty\\cat.py","firedalazer")
| summarize PollCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP
| where PollCount >= 4
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationHostName =~ "api.github.com" or RequestURL has "api.github.com"
| where RequestURL has "/search/commits" or RequestURL has "firedalazer"
| where RequestClientApplication startswith "python-requests"
| summarize PollCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleUrls = make_set(RequestURL, 5)
          by SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestClientApplication
| where PollCount >= 4
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR */python OR */python3) @DestinationHostname:api.github.com @CommandLine:(*cat.py* OR *kitty* OR *firedalazer*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^api\.github\.com$/i ContextImageFileName=/python(3)?(\.exe)?$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/(cat\.py|kitty[\\\/]cat\.py|\.local[\\\/]share[\\\/]kitty|firedalazer)/i}, field=ContextProcessId, key=TargetProcessId, include=[CommandLine])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| _count >= 4

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud GitHub dead-drop exfiltration via python-requests/2.31.0 Actions on Objectives High
Detects POST/PUT to api.github.com from a python-requests/2.31.0 User-Agent creating Dune-themed repositories or committing 'results-<timestamp>-<counter>.json' files. This is the article's secondary exfil channel activated when the malware harvests a developer's GitHub PAT, used to stash AES-256-GCM-encrypted credential dumps. Rationale: Anchored on the article's three concrete IOCs: User-Agent string 'python-requests/2.31.0', the exfil filename pattern 'results/results-<timestamp>-<counter>.json', and the Dune-themed repo naming convention (sardaukar/fremen/atreides + sandworm/ornithopter/stillsuit). Triple-anchor (UA + method + path keyword) keeps FP rate well below a generic python-requests-to-github hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1567 T1102.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SuspiciousPython = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3.exe","python3")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py",".local/share/kitty","kitty\\cat.py")
    | project DeviceId, ProcessId, PyStart=Timestamp, PyCmd=ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3.exe","python3")
| join kind=inner SuspiciousPython on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ProcessId
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 5), SampleCmd = any(PyCmd)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationHostName =~ "api.github.com"
| where RequestClientApplication startswith "python-requests/2.31"
| where RequestMethod in ("POST","PUT","PATCH")
| where RequestURL has_any ("/user/repos","/contents/results-","sardaukar","fremen","atreides","sandworm","ornithopter","stillsuit","harkonnen")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, SentBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

            - 'wget '

            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

How Storm-2949 turned a compromised identity into a cloud-wide breach

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-05-18 20 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Storm-2949 turned stolen credentials into a cloud-wide breach, moving from identity compromise to large-scale data theft without using malware. This incident shows how threat actors can exploit trusted systems to operate undetected. The post How Storm-2949 turned a compromised identity into a cloud-wide breach appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ATT&CKT1059.001 T1190 T1204.002 T1219 T1486 T1528 T1539 T1566
IPs176.123.4.44 91.208.197.87 185.241.208.243

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Storm-2949 Microsoft Graph API tenant enumeration via cURL / Python user-agent
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Sign-in from Storm-2949 attacker egress IPs (176.123.4.44 / 91.208.197.87 / 185.241.208.243) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Storm-2949 SSPR + MFA-method swap sequence (password reset followed by attacker MFA registration) · [LLM] Defender Antivirus tamper attempts from compromised-identity Azure VM session · [LLM] Service principal credential added by user (Storm-2949 SP persistence attempt) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ScreenConnect outbound connection to Storm-2949 C2 (185.241.208.243) from Azure VM · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Storm-2949 OneDrive / SharePoint bulk file download (mass-exfil pattern) · [LLM] Azure Key Vault secret extraction by user identity (Storm-2949 credential-access pattern) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Sign-in from Storm-2949 attacker egress IPs (176.123.4.44 / 91.208.197.87 / 185.241.208.243) Delivery High
Detects interactive and non-interactive Entra ID sign-ins originating from the three IPs Microsoft attributed to Storm-2949 (two egress IPs plus the ScreenConnect host). Article-specific because it pivots on the exact IOC IPs from the MSRC blog's IOC table. Rationale: Uses the three IPs in MSRC's official IOC table verbatim. Two are attacker egress, one is the ScreenConnect host — any successful sign-in from these is high-fidelity TP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1556.006

  (AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where IPAddress in ("176.123.4.44","91.208.197.87","185.241.208.243") | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName, IPAddress, ResultType, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ClientAppUsed)

[LLM] Storm-2949 SSPR + MFA-method swap sequence (password reset followed by attacker MFA registration) Installation High
Detects the Storm-2949 persistence pattern: an SSPR-driven password reset immediately followed by removal of the user's existing MFA methods and registration of a new authenticator within minutes. This is the article's signature persistence move. Rationale: Microsoft's writeup explicitly describes the chain as SSPR → password reset → remove existing MFA methods → register attacker's Authenticator. Joining password-reset and security-info-register events in a 15m window catches that exact sequence without alerting on benign solo password resets. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-sspr-deployment
ATT&CKT1556.006 T1098.005
Data sourcesChange.Auth
// Defender Advanced Hunting doesn't expose AuditLogs directly — use CloudAppEvents proxy
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Azure Active Directory"
| where ActionType in ("Reset user password (self-service)","User registered security info","User deleted security info","Update user")
| extend TargetUpn = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
| summarize Ops = make_set(ActionType), OpCount = dcount(ActionType), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), IPs = make_set(IPAddress) by AccountObjectId, TargetUpn, bin(Timestamp, 15m)
| where OpCount >= 2 and Ops has "Reset user password (self-service)" and Ops has "User registered security info"
| order by FirstSeen desc
let Window = 15m;
let PwdResets = AuditLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where OperationName in ("Reset user password (self-service)","Reset password (self-service)")
  | extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
  | project ResetTime = TimeGenerated, TargetUpn, Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), CorrelationId;
let MfaChanges = AuditLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where OperationName in ("User registered security info","User deleted security info","Admin registered security info")
  | extend TargetUpn = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName)
  | project MfaTime = TimeGenerated, TargetUpn, MfaOp = OperationName;
PwdResets
| join kind=inner MfaChanges on TargetUpn
| where MfaTime between (ResetTime .. ResetTime + Window)
| summarize Ops = make_set(MfaOp), FirstMfa = min(MfaTime), LastMfa = max(MfaTime) by TargetUpn, ResetTime, Initiator, CorrelationId
| where Ops has "User registered security info"
| order by ResetTime desc
source:azure.activeDirectory (@evt.name:"Reset user password (self-service)" OR @evt.name:"User registered security info" OR @evt.name:"User deleted security info")
CLOUD
`azure_audit` (OperationName="Reset user password (self-service)" OR OperationName="User registered security info" OR OperationName="User deleted security info") | bin _time span=15m | stats values(OperationName) as ops dc(OperationName) as op_kinds values(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName) as upn min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by TargetResources{}.userPrincipalName | where op_kinds>=2 AND mvfind(ops,"Reset user password")>=0 AND mvfind(ops,"User registered security info")>=0
[LLM] Storm-2949 Microsoft Graph API tenant enumeration via cURL / Python user-agent Reconnaissance Medium
Detects the article's custom-Python directory-discovery script enumerating users and applications via Graph. Pivots on non-browser user agents (python-requests/, curl/) calling graph.microsoft.com /users and /applications. Rationale: Article states attacker used a custom Python script issuing automated Graph API requests to enumerate users and applications. Non-browser UA on Graph from a regular-user identity is a strong, narrow signal that wouldn't trip on legitimate Power Automate / Power BI sign-ins. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/004/
ATT&CKT1087.004 T1069.003
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ResourceDisplayName == "Microsoft Graph"
| where UserAgent matches regex @"(?i)^(python-requests|curl|go-http-client|powershell|aiohttp|httpx)/"
| summarize Calls = count(), UAs = make_set(UserAgent), IPs = make_set(IPAddress), Apps = make_set(Application), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by AccountUpn
| where Calls >= 10
| order by Calls desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where ResourceDisplayName == "Microsoft Graph" | where UserAgent matches regex @"(?i)^(python-requests|curl|go-http-client|powershell|aiohttp|httpx)/" | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, UserAgent, IPAddress, AppDisplayName),
  (AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where ResourceDisplayName == "Microsoft Graph" | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, AppDisplayName)
| summarize Calls = count(), UAs = make_set(UserAgent), IPs = make_set(IPAddress), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName) by UserPrincipalName
| where Calls >= 10
| order by Calls desc

  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    ResourceDisplayName: 'Microsoft Graph'
    UserAgent|startswith:
      - 'python-requests/'
      - 'curl/'
      - 'Go-http-client/'
      - 'aiohttp/'
      - 'httpx/'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:azure.activeDirectory @properties.resourceDisplayName:"Microsoft Graph" (@http.useragent:python-requests\/* OR @http.useragent:curl\/* OR @http.useragent:Go-http-client\/* OR @http.useragent:aiohttp\/* OR @http.useragent:httpx\/*)
CLOUD
`azure_signin` ResourceDisplayName="Microsoft Graph" UserAgent IN ("python-requests/*","curl/*","PowerShell/*","Go-http-client/*") | stats count dc(UserAgent) as ua_variants values(UserAgent) as agents values(IPAddress) as srcip values(AppDisplayName) as app by UserPrincipalName | where count>=10
[LLM] Storm-2949 OneDrive / SharePoint bulk file download (mass-exfil pattern) Actions on Objectives High
Detects the article's described OneDrive web-interface mass-download — thousands of files in a single user action to attacker infrastructure. Correlates user FileDownloaded operations with a high distinct-file threshold over a short window. Rationale: Article: "Storm-2949 used the OneDrive web interface to download thousands of files in a single action." The 200-file/15m threshold (~13 files/min sustained) is well above typical user sync behaviour and matches the bulk-action shape described. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/defender/advanced-hunting-cloudappevents-table
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1530
Data sourcesWeb
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application in ("Microsoft OneDrive for Business","Microsoft SharePoint Online")
| where ActionType in ("FileDownloaded","FileSyncDownloadedFull")
| summarize FileCount = dcount(ObjectName), Sites = dcount(tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).SiteUrl)), IPs = make_set(IPAddress), UAs = make_set(UserAgent), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, bin(Timestamp, 15m)
| where FileCount >= 200
| extend DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by FileCount desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload in ("OneDrive","SharePoint")
| where Operation in ("FileDownloaded","FileSyncDownloadedFull")
| summarize FileCount = dcount(ObjectId), Sites = dcount(Site_Url), IPs = make_set(ClientIP), UAs = make_set(UserAgent), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by UserId, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where FileCount >= 200
| extend DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| order by FileCount desc
source:office365 (@evt.name:FileDownloaded OR @evt.name:FileSyncDownloadedFull) (@OfficeWorkload:OneDrive OR @OfficeWorkload:SharePoint)
APPLICATION
`o365_management_activity` Workload="OneDrive" OR Workload="SharePoint" Operation IN ("FileDownloaded","FileSyncDownloadedFull") | bucket _time span=15m | stats dc(ObjectId) as files dc(Site_Url) as sites values(ClientIP) as ip values(UserAgent) as ua min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by UserId _time | where files>=200
[LLM] ScreenConnect outbound connection to Storm-2949 C2 (185.241.208.243) from Azure VM Command & Control High
Detects an Azure VM (or any onboarded endpoint) calling out to 185.241.208.243, the ScreenConnect host Storm-2949 used per Microsoft's IOC table. Also flags ScreenConnect process artifacts on hosts that shouldn't have remote-support tooling. Rationale: 185.241.208.243 is the exact ScreenConnect host IP from Microsoft's IOC table. The article specifically calls out "ScreenConnect installed on Azure VM" as the persistence move in the Azure compromise phase, so process-name matches on ScreenConnect.* binaries are equally high-fidelity in environments where ScreenConnect isn't sanctioned RMM. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1219 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where RemoteIP == "185.241.208.243" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn),
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)^(ScreenConnect|connectwise)" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("screenconnect.client.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","ConnectWise Control") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceNetworkEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where RemoteIP == "185.241.208.243" | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn),
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr == "185.241.208.243" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol),
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationIP == "185.241.208.243" | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, SourceUserName),
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)screenconnect|connectwise" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Storm-2949 ScreenConnect C2 outbound (185.241.208.243)

(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:185.241.208.243) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe OR *\\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe OR *\\screenconnect.clientservice.exe))) OR (source:cloudtrail @network.client.ip:185.241.208.243)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dport values(All_Traffic.src) as src values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest="185.241.208.243" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
[LLM] Defender Antivirus tamper attempts from compromised-identity Azure VM session Installation High
Detects the article's defense-evasion step: attacker attempts to turn off Microsoft Defender Antivirus on a VM under compromised-identity context (Set-MpPreference DisableRealtimeMonitoring, exclusion-path additions, tamper-protection toggles). Rationale: Article IOC table calls out "Attempts to tamper with Microsoft Defender Antivirus" under Defense Evasion. Regex covers the canonical Defender-kill commands seen in T1562.001 reporting (Set-MpPreference, exclusions, WinDefend/Sense service stop). Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-attack-surface-reduction
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","reg.exe","sc.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(Set-MpPreference\s+.*DisableRealtimeMonitoring|Set-MpPreference\s+.*-ExclusionPath|Add-MpPreference\s+.*-ExclusionProcess|Set-MpPreference\s+.*-DisableIOAVProtection|DisableAntiSpyware|sc\s+(stop|config)\s+WinDefend|sc\s+(stop|config)\s+Sense)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","reg.exe","sc.exe") | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(Set-MpPreference\s+.*DisableRealtimeMonitoring|Set-MpPreference\s+.*-ExclusionPath|Add-MpPreference\s+.*-ExclusionProcess|DisableAntiSpyware|sc\s+(stop|config)\s+WinDefend|sc\s+(stop|config)\s+Sense)" | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountUpn, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn),
  (SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where EventID == 4688 | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(Set-MpPreference\s+.*DisableRealtimeMonitoring|Add-MpPreference\s+.*-ExclusionPath|DisableAntiSpyware|sc\s+(stop|config)\s+WinDefend)" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Defender AV tamper via PowerShell / sc.exe / reg.exe
id: e2a9c5a1-7b1c-4c8e-9f37-58d40a2c1b22
description: Disable Microsoft Defender Antivirus real-time protection, add process/path exclusions, or stop WinDefend/Sense services — Storm-2949 defense-evasion tradecraft on compromised Azure VMs.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\reg.exe'
      - '\sc.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring'
      - 'Set-MpPreference -ExclusionPath'
      - 'Add-MpPreference -ExclusionProcess'
      - 'Set-MpPreference -DisableIOAVProtection'
      - 'DisableAntiSpyware'
      - 'sc stop WinDefend'
      - 'sc config WinDefend'
      - 'sc stop Sense'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\sc.exe OR *\\reg.exe) (@CommandLine:*DisableRealtimeMonitoring* OR @CommandLine:*"-ExclusionPath"* OR @CommandLine:*"-ExclusionProcess"* OR @CommandLine:*DisableAntiSpyware* OR @CommandLine:*"sc stop WinDefend"* OR @CommandLine:*"sc config WinDefend"* OR @CommandLine:*"sc stop Sense"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|reg|sc)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(Set-MpPreference\\s+.*DisableRealtimeMonitoring|Set-MpPreference\\s+.*-ExclusionPath|Add-MpPreference\\s+.*-ExclusionProcess|DisableAntiSpyware|sc\\s+(stop|config)\\s+WinDefend|sc\\s+(stop|config)\\s+Sense)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*-ExclusionPath*" OR Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*-ExclusionProcess*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*-DisableIOAVProtection*" OR Processes.process="*sc*config*WinDefend*" OR Processes.process="*reg*add*DisableAntiSpyware*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*DisableRealtimeMonitoring*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*-ExclusionPath*" OR Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*-ExclusionProcess*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*-DisableIOAVProtection*" OR Processes.process="*sc*config*WinDefend*" OR Processes.process="*reg*add*DisableAntiSpyware*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] Azure Key Vault secret extraction by user identity (Storm-2949 credential-access pattern) Actions on Objectives High
Detects a regular-user identity (not a service principal or app) issuing high-volume secret/key/cert GET or LIST operations against Azure Key Vault — the article's credential-access step where Storm-2949 extracted secrets from Key Vault using compromised RBAC. Rationale: Article IOC table calls out "Secret extraction from Azure Key Vault" under Credential Access. Filtering on user UPN (not appId) excludes legitimate apps reading their own secrets, and the 20-call / 5-distinct-secret threshold catches enumeration-style access patterns vs. one-off interactive reads. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/logging • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/006/
ATT&CKT1555.006 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange Authentication
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT"
| where Category == "AuditEvent"
| where OperationName in ("SecretGet","SecretList","KeyGet","KeyList","CertificateGet","CertificateList")
| extend CallerUpn = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).identity.claim["http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/upn"])
| extend CallerAppId = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).identity.claim.appid)
| extend CallerIp = tostring(parse_json(tostring(Properties)).clientInfo.ipAddress)
| where isnotempty(CallerUpn)   // user identity, not pure SPN
| summarize Calls = count(), DistinctSecrets = dcount(Resource), Ops = make_set(OperationName), Vaults = make_set(Resource), IPs = make_set(CallerIp), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by CallerUpn, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
| where Calls >= 20 or DistinctSecrets >= 5
| order by Calls desc
source:azure.activity_logs @resource.type:Microsoft.KeyVault\/vaults (@operationName.value:Microsoft.KeyVault\/vaults\/secrets\/getSecret\/action OR @operationName.value:Microsoft.KeyVault\/vaults\/secrets\/readMetadata\/action OR @operationName.value:Microsoft.KeyVault\/vaults\/keys\/read\/action) @identity.claim.upn:*
CLOUD
`azure_keyvault_audit` (OperationName="SecretGet" OR OperationName="SecretList" OR OperationName="KeyGet" OR OperationName="CertificateGet" OR OperationName="VaultGet") identity_claim_appid=null | stats count dc(id_s) as distinct_secrets values(identity_claim_upn) as upn values(CallerIPAddress) as ip min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by identity_claim_upn KeyVaultName | where count>=20 OR distinct_secrets>=5
[LLM] Service principal credential added by user (Storm-2949 SP persistence attempt) Installation High
Detects a user identity adding a new client secret or certificate credential to a service principal — the article's specific (failed) persistence attempt. Even if Storm-2949's attempt failed, the operation pattern is high-fidelity for SP-takeover persistence. Rationale: Article: "the threat actor also attempted to establish persistence by adding credentials to a compromised service principal" — this is literally the operation name to detect. Filter on `Initiator` non-empty to scope to user-driven (vs. SPN-to-SPN automation) cred adds. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/18/storm-2949-turned-compromised-identity-into-cloud-wide-breach/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1098/001/
ATT&CKT1098.001
Data sourcesChange
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Azure Active Directory"
| where ActionType in ("Add service principal credentials","Update application – Certificates and secrets management","Update service principal")
| extend Initiator = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend TargetSp = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).TargetResources[0].displayName)
| where isnotempty(Initiator)   // exclude SP-on-SP credential adds (Graph automation)
| project Timestamp, Initiator, TargetSp, ActionType, IPAddress, AccountObjectId
| order by Timestamp desc
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in ("Add service principal credentials","Update application – Certificates and secrets management","Update service principal")
| extend Initiator = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InitiatorIp = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetSp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend TargetAppId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| where isnotempty(Initiator)   // exclude SP-to-SP automation
| project TimeGenerated, Initiator, InitiatorIp, TargetSp, TargetAppId, OperationName, Result, ResultReason, CorrelationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Service principal credential added by user identity (T1098.001)

CLOUD
`azure_audit` (OperationName="Add service principal credentials" OR OperationName="Update application – Certificates and secrets management" OR OperationName="Update service principal") | stats count values(TargetResources{}.displayName) as sp_name values(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName) as upn values(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress) as ip min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by InitiatedBy.user.id
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

SecurityEvent

   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/

            - '\psexesvc.exe'

            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

AuditLogs

| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] mistralai 2.4.6 dropper: curl downloading transformers.pyz from 83.142.209.194 Delivery High
Detects the first-stage download performed by the malicious _run_background_task function in mistralai 2.4.6 — a curl invocation with TLS verification disabled (-k) fetching transformers.pyz from the hard-coded attacker IP 83.142.209.194. The combination of binary, flags, target IP, and output filename is unique to this campaign. Rationale: Combines three high-fidelity strings from the article: the literal C2 IP (83.142.209.194), the dropped filename (transformers.pyz), and the curl binary. Each on its own would be specific; the conjunction is unique to this campaign. The python parent and -k (TLS-verify-off) flag are additional confirming pivots from the dropper code reproduced verbatim in GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg • https://github.com/mistralai/client-python/issues/523 • https://pypi.org/project/mistralai/
ATT&CKT1105 T1195.002 T1573.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "curl"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "83.142.209.194"
     or (ProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz" and ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/")
| extend TlsVerifyDisabled = ProcessCommandLine has " -k" or ProcessCommandLine has "--insecure"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          TlsVerifyDisabled, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DvcOs has_any ("linux", "Linux")
| where TargetProcessName has "curl"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "83.142.209.194"
     or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "transformers.pyz" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/")
| extend TlsVerifyDisabled = TargetProcessCommandLine has " -k" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "--insecure"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TlsVerifyDisabled
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious mistralai 2.4.6 PyPI Dropper - Curl Download of transformers.pyz from 83.142.209.194
id: 9c4f8e2a-1b3d-4f5e-8a7b-2c9d0e1f3a4b
description: Detects the first-stage curl download performed by the malicious _run_background_task function added to mistralai==2.4.6 on PyPI, which fetches /tmp/transformers.pyz from the attacker-controlled IP 83.142.209.194 with TLS verification disabled.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg
  - https://github.com/mistralai/client-python/issues/523
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '/curl'
  selection_indicators:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '83.142.209.194'
      - 'transformers.pyz'
  condition: selection_img and selection_indicators
falsepositives:
  - None expected — this is a hard IOC match against a campaign-specific IP and filename combination.
level: critical
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:curl OR @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */CURL)) (@process.command_line:*83.142.209.194* OR @process.command_line:*transformers.pyz*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/curl$/i (CommandLine=/83\.142\.209\.194/ or CommandLine=/transformers\.pyz/)
| ParentBaseFileName=/^python[0-9.]*$/i OR CommandLine=/\s-k\s/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="curl" (Processes.process="*83.142.209.194*" OR Processes.process="*transformers.pyz*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where (match(parent_process_name, "^python[0-9.]*$") OR like(process, "%-k%-L%-s%")) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] mistralai 2.4.6 dropper: Python interpreter executing /tmp/transformers.pyz as detached session Installation High
Detects the second stage of the mistralai 2.4.6 supply-chain dropper — a python interpreter (sys.executable) executing the dropped /tmp/transformers.pyz zipapp. The python-runs-pyz-from-tmp pattern is the actual code-execution moment; combined with /tmp/ the false-positive rate is near zero. Rationale: Built directly on the Popen invocation in the GHSA's reproduced source: Popen([sys.executable, '/tmp/transformers.pyz'], start_new_session=True). Python interpreter running a .pyz from /tmp is itself unusual; the exact filename transformers.pyz makes this a campaign IOC. The python-parent-spawning-python relationship is the byproduct of subprocess.Popen with sys.executable. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg • https://github.com/mistralai/client-python/issues/523
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1195.002 T1106
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName matches regex @"^python[0-9.]*$"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/transformers.pyz"
     or (ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/[^\s]+\.pyz(\s|$)")
| extend ParentIsPython = InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^python[0-9.]*$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentIsPython
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DvcOs has_any ("linux", "Linux")
| where TargetProcessName matches regex @"python[0-9.]*$"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/transformers.pyz"
     or (TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/[^\s]+\.pyz(\s|$)")
| extend ParentIsPython = ActingProcessName matches regex @"python[0-9.]*$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentIsPython
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious mistralai 2.4.6 PyPI Dropper - Python Executing /tmp/transformers.pyz Zipapp
id: 7d3e5b1c-8a2f-4c6d-9e0a-1f5b3c7d2e4a
description: Detects the second-stage execution of the mistralai 2.4.6 supply-chain dropper — a python interpreter executing the dropped zipapp at /tmp/transformers.pyz. The function _run_background_task in src/mistralai/client/__init__.py invokes Popen([sys.executable, '/tmp/transformers.pyz'], start_new_session=True).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg
  - https://github.com/mistralai/client-python/issues/523
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_python:
    Image|re: 'python[0-9.]*$'
  selection_pyz:
    CommandLine|contains: '/tmp/transformers.pyz'
  condition: selection_python and selection_pyz
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use of Python zipapps stored in /tmp is highly unusual and the file name 'transformers.pyz' is campaign-specific.

[LLM] Outbound network connection to mistralai 2.4.6 dropper C2 (83.142.209.194) Command & Control High
Detects any host in the estate establishing an outbound connection to the attacker-controlled IP 83.142.209.194 referenced in GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg as the host serving the second-stage transformers.pyz payload. Any connection to this IP is high-confidence evidence the dropper-download stage ran. Rationale: Pure IOC-match on the C2 IP referenced verbatim in the GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg advisory and reproduced from public issue #523. Hardcoded into the dropper at https://83.142.209.194/transformers.pyz — any tenant connection to this IP is by definition this campaign. Pivot to InitiatingProcessFileName/Command to identify whether curl, python, or another binary did the call (telemetry vendor varies). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg • https://github.com/mistralai/client-python/issues/523
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "83.142.209.194"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp asc
union isfuzzy=true
(
  ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr == "83.142.209.194"
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername,
            DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkBytes,
            Url, EventProduct
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP == "83.142.209.194"
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName=SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP,
            DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct
)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] Drop of /tmp/transformers.pyz on Linux endpoint Installation High
Detects creation of the dropper artifact /tmp/transformers.pyz on disk — the specific filename and path written by the malicious mistralai 2.4.6 _run_background_task function. Even if the second-stage execution fails or is killed, the file write is a definitive forensic indicator the dropper ran. Rationale: Hard-IOC match on the exact filename + path written by the dropper code reproduced in the GHSA: curl ... -o /tmp/transformers.pyz. This persists on disk even if MISTRAL_INIT is set (which prevents re-download but doesn't delete the file). The advisory explicitly recommends `ls -la /tmp/transformers.pyz` as the affected-host check — this UC is the telemetry-side equivalent. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wx9m-wx4f-4cmg • https://github.com/mistralai/client-python/issues/523
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "transformers.pyz"
| where FolderPath in~ ("/tmp", "/tmp/") or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          FileOriginIP, FileOriginUrl
| order by Timestamp asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "transformers.pyz"
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/" or TargetFilePath == "/tmp/transformers.pyz"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated asc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b") or SHA1 in~ ("6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b") or MD5 in~ ("6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b") or SHA1 in~ ("6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b") or MD5 in~ ("6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6dbaa43bf2f3c0d3cddbca74967e952da563fb974c1ef9d4ecbb2e58e41fe81b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
